bullets: Soil erosion patterns on race tracks directly influence trajectory choices between practice and race day, making track condition awareness a core racing strategy.
Tire pressure and casing selection matter more than minor suspension adjustments, as they impact grip and stability on eroded terrain.
Speed comes from braking earlier and more smoothly rather than taking greater risks, a principle observed across multiple teams using RockShox.
The framing of a race setup reveals the compromises being made — design decisions reflect tradeoffs in risk, durability, and performance.
Risk management in enduro racing isn't about avoiding crashes but about choosing which crashes are survivable through disciplined technique.
The Cascadia Alliance highlights how second-order effects — like altered rider behavior due to track erosion — shape long-term race outcomes.
Spoke & Wrench integration into team workflows makes the trade-off between risk and reliability visibly apparent across three observed teams.
Listeners should implement one core idea from the episode for two weeks to test its impact — everything else is iteration.
